title: Index and stock futures: mechanics
objectives: Describe contract specifications and the long/short payoff.
body_md:
## Contract basics

- Each contract has a **lot size**, an **expiry date**, a **tick size** and an underlying. Lot sizes and expiries are revised by the exchanges: check current circulars.
- A **long** future profits when the price rises; a **short** when it falls.
- **Payoff at expiry (long)** = (spot at expiry − entry price) × lot size.

## Margins

| Margin | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Initial margin** | Collateral to open a position, based on risk (SPAN plus exposure) |
| **Mark-to-market (MTM) margin** | Daily settlement of gains and losses |
| **Margin call** | Demand to top up if the balance falls |

## Example

Buy 1 lot (lot = 50) at 20,000. The close is 20,100: MTM gain = 100 × 50 = ₹5,000 credited. If the next close is 19,950, loss = 150 × 50 = ₹7,500 debited.

## Settlement

Index futures settle in **cash**; stock futures are **physically settled** under the current framework (verify).

> **Exam tip:** Futures P&L is realised every day through MTM.
example: Long 2 lots (lot = 25) at ₹1,000. Expiry price ₹1,040. Profit = 40 × 25 × 2 = ₹2,000.
